egress.terms: 'Monthly Usenet Data Unlimited' on the Unlimited and XL plans, 50 GB on Lite. No speed cap is stated; connections are 30 on Lite and 100 on the other two.

tooling: Every usenet client: SABnzbd, NZBGet, nzbget-compatible downloaders, spotweb. No provider-side API is needed or offered.
chaining: The Unlimited plan is the feed behind a debrid or *arr stack: 100 connections and 6676 days of retention are what make an old post still downloadable, and 'Unlimited Data' is the only uncapped byte path in this whole lane.

notes: The charged price has not moved in 36 months; what changed is that the vendor began publishing a list price of $19.94 in 2025 that it then discounts to $12.95. The page does not say whether a renewal bills $12.95 or $19.94, and the honest reading is that $12.95 is the price as long as the promotion runs - so the exposure is 54% on renewal, not a discount that can be banked. This is the largest published promo-versus-list gap in the set after Eweka. Potential failure points: retention (refuted for time-based expiry by the vendor's own sentence), takedown removal (confirmed as a stated cause), or connection count (documented as a plan property, no number read). A client that pulls older releases meets removal far more often than age. The DMCA/NTD split is a third party's inference from server location and notices, not a published rule. Cheapest Omicron entry seen on any of its storefronts was a 15-month promo at $1.99/mo quoted by a third-party deals page, not by the vendor, so it is not documented as a price here.

extras.promo_gap: charged USD 12.95 against a published list of USD 19.94: the list is 54.0% higher than the charge
extras.renewal_price: not published; the page shows only the struck list price and the charged price
extras.account_states: credential refusal is 481/482/502 at connect; the page read covers article-level states only
extras.cache_miss: not applicable: an article either exists on the spool or answers 430
extras.takedown_path: removal by legal notice, reported by the vendor as one of the two causes of 430; no per-article status distinguishes it from age
extras.host_removal: not applicable; the equivalent event is a backbone dropping a group or an article

identity_cost.kind.reason: pricing-history's detail says 'card payment' while its kind says email, and usenet-providers says a card is required before the first byte because there is no trial. No lane names a non-card rail, so the more restrictive value is the evidenced one.

verdict.reason: Merged value stands. No free tier and no trial; the 30-day guarantee refunds a payment rather than avoiding one. failure-modes' 'qualifies' claims a free path that does not exist.

binding.reason: The record prices the Unlimited tier, which publishes no byte counter, no speed cap and no fair-use figure, so nothing in the vocabulary fails at 1 TiB/month; 100 connections is concurrency, not a byte ceiling. The merged volume-quota reads the 50 GB cap of the Lite plan, which is a different plan and would need its own tier record.

interface_detail: Access is NNTP over TLS (port 563). The schema's interface enum has no nntp token, so this is documented as unknown rather than mislabelled as rest or cli; the real interface is a standard protocol every usenet client speaks.
limits_note: The 6676-day retention figure is the vendor's own and is the same on all three plans; it is a property of the article store, not a quota.
binding_note: Lite's 50 GB/month is exhausted in under two hours at 1 TiB/month, so the plan choice is the binding decision. Unlimited removes the byte counter and leaves connection count as the only ceiling.
confidence_note: Four dated reads, three archived. The $12.95 has not moved; the strike-through list price appears only from 2025.
